implementation_notes: TypeScript uses the same package as JavaScript and adds the type layer: new PactV3({consumer, provider, dir}) together with the fluent interaction chain and MatchersV3 is fully typed, so an interaction can be pinned to the request and response interfaces the client actually uses, and the typed Verifier drives provider verification; jest-pact removes the fixture boilerplate and the repository ships TypeScript examples under examples/e2e/v3/typescript. The types do not change the mechanics - the mock server still validates the real client's request - so the value is catching request-shape mistakes at compile time rather than at verification time.
pitfalls: Types vanish at runtime: an interface narrower than the payload the client sends still compiles, and only the mock server's request assertions catch the mismatch.
Bodies passed straight into willRespondWith are matched exactly, so a provider field addition fails verification until the body is wrapped in MatchersV3.like/eachLike.
An interaction is identified by its description, not by the test name, so two tests reusing one description overwrite each other's contract entry.
